1.1: And it comes to pass, in the days of the judging of the judges, that there is a famine in the land, and there goes a man from Beth-Lehem-Judah to sojourn in the fields of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons.
1.2: And the name of the man is Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi, and the name of his two sons Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites from Beth-Lehem-Judah; and they come into the fields of Moab, and are there.
1.3: And Elimelech husband of Naomi dies, and she is left, she and her two sons;
1.4: and they take to them wives, Moabitesses: the name of the one is Orpah, and the name of the second Ruth; and they dwell there about ten years.
1.5: And they die also, both of them--Mahlon and Chilion--and the woman is left of her two children and of her husband.
1.6: And she rises, she and her daughters-in-law, and turns back from the fields of Moab, for she has heard in the fields of Moab that God has looked after His people, --to give to them bread.
1.7: And she goes out from the place where she has been, and her two daughters-in-law with her, and they go in the way to turn back to the land of Judah.
1.8: And Naomi says to her two daughters-in-law, `Go, turn back, each to the house of her mother; Jehovah does with you kindness as you have done with the dead, and with me;
1.9: Jehovah does grant to you, and find you rest each in the house of her husband;' and she kisses them, and they lift up their voice and weep.
1.10: And they say to her, `Surely with you we go back to your people.'
1.11: And Naomi says, `Turn back, my daughters; why do you go with me? are there yet to me sons in my bowels that they have been to you for husbands?
1.12: Turn back, my daughters, go, for I am too aged to be to a husband; though I had said, There is for me hope, also, I have been to-night to a husband, and also I have borne sons:
1.13: for them do you wait till that they grow up? for them do you shut yourselves up, not to be to a husband? no, my daughters, for more bitter to me than to you, for the hand of Jehovah has gone out against me.'
1.14: And they lift up their voice, and weep again, and Orpah kisses her mother-in-law, and Ruth has cleaved to her.
1.15: And she says, `Indeed, your sister-in-law has turned back to her people, and to her god, turn you back after your sister-in-law.'
1.16: And Ruth says, `Urge me not to leave you--to turn back from after you; for where you go I go, and where you lodge I lodge; your people is my people, and your God my God.
1.17: Where you die I die, and there I am buried; thus does Jehovah to me, and thus does He add--for death itself does part between me and you.'
1.18: And she sees that she is strengthening herself to go with her, and she ceases to speak to her;
1.19: and they go both of them till their coming in to Beth-Lehem; and it comes to pass at their coming in to Beth-Lehem, that all the city is moved at them, and they say, `Is this Naomi?'
1.20: And she says to them, `Call me not Naomi; call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly to me,
1.21: I went out full, and empty has Jehovah brought me back, why do you call me Naomi, and Jehovah has testified against me, and the Almighty has done evil to me?'
1.22: And Naomi turns back, and Ruth the Moabitess her daughter-in-law with her, who has turned back from the fields of Moab, and they have come in to Beth-Lehem at the commencement of barley-harvest.

2.1: And Naomi has an acquaintance of her husband's, a man mighty in wealth, of the family of Elimelech, and his name is Boaz.
2.2: And Ruth the Moabitess says to Naomi, `Let me go, I pray you, into the field, and I gather among the ears of corn after him in whose eyes I find grace;' and she says to her, `Go, my daughter.'
2.3: And she goes and comes and gathers in a field after the reapers, and her chance happens--the portion of the field is Boaz's who is of the family of Elimelech.
2.4: And indeed, Boaz has come from Beth-Lehem, and says to the reapers, `Jehovah is with you;' and they say to him, `Jehovah does bless you.'
2.5: And Boaz says to his young man who is set over the reapers, `Whose is this young person?'
2.6: And the young man who is set over the reapers answers and says, `A young woman--Moabitess--she is, who came back with Naomi from the fields of Moab,
2.7: and she says, Let me glean, I pray you--and I have gathered among the sheaves after the reapers; and she comes and remains since the morning and till now; she sat in the house a little.
2.8: And Boaz says to Ruth, `Have you not heard, my daughter? go not to glean in another field, and also, pass not over from this, and thus you do cleave to my young women:
2.9: your eyes are on the field which they reap, and you have gone after them; have not I charged the young men not to touch you? when you are athirst then you have gone to the vessels, and have drunk from that which the young men draw.'
2.10: And she falls on her face, and bows herself to the earth, and says to him, `Wherefore have I found grace in your eyes, to discern me, and I a stranger?'
2.11: And Boaz answers and says to her, `It has thoroughly been declared to me all that you have done with your mother-in-law, after the death of your husband, and you do leave your father, and your mother, and the land of your birth, and do come in to a people which you have not known heretofore.
2.12: Jehovah does recompense your work, and your reward is complete from Jehovah, God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.'
2.13: And she says, `Let me find grace in your eyes, my lord, because you have comforted me, and because you have spoken to the heart of your maid-servant, and I--I am not as one of your maid-servants.'
2.14: And Boaz says to her, `At meal-time come nigh here, and you have eaten of the bread, and dipped your morsel in the vinegar.' And she sits at the side of the reapers, and he reaches to her roasted corn, and she eats, and is satisfied, and leaves.
2.15: And she rises to glean, and Boaz charges his young men, saying, `Even between the sheaves she does glean, and you do not cause her to blush;
2.16: and also you do surely cast to her of the handfuls--and have left, and she has gleaned, and you do not push against her.'
2.17: And she gleans in the field till the evening, and beats out that which she has gleaned, and it is about an ephah of barley;
2.18: and she takes it up, and goes into the city, and her mother-in-law sees that which she has gleaned, and she brings out and gives to her that which she left from her satiety.
2.19: And her mother-in-law says to her, `Where have you gleaned to-day? and where have you worked? may he who is discerning you be blessed.' And she declares to her mother-in-law with whom she has worked, and says, `The name of the man with whom I have worked to-day is Boaz.'
2.20: And Naomi says to her daughter-in-law, `Blessed is he of Jehovah who has not forsaken His kindness with the living and with the dead;' and Naomi says to her, `The man is a relation of ours; he is of our redeemers.'
2.21: And Ruth the Moabitess says, `Also he surely said to me, Near the young people whom I have you do cleave till they have completed the whole of the harvest which I have.'
2.22: And Naomi says to Ruth her daughter-in-law, `Good, my daughter, that you go out with his young women, and they come not against you in another field.'
2.23: And she cleaves to the young women of Boaz to glean, till the completion of the barley-harvest, and of the wheat-harvest, and she dwells with her mother-in-law.

3.1: And Naomi her mother-in-law says to her, `My daughter, do not I seek for you rest, that it may be well with you?
3.2: and now, is not Boaz of our acquaintance, with whose young women you have been? indeed, he is winnowing the threshing-floor of barley to-night,
3.3: and you have bathed, and anointed yourself, and put your garments upon you, and gone down to the threshing-floor; let not yourself be known to the man till he complete to eat and to drink;
3.4: and it comes to pass when he lies down, that you have known the place where he lies down, and have gone in, and uncovered his feet, and lain down, --and he does declare to you that which you do do.'
3.5: And she says to her, `All that you say--I do.'
3.6: And she goes down to the threshing-floor, and does according to all that her mother-in-law commanded her
3.7: And Boaz eats and drinks, and his heart is glad; and he goes in to lie down at the end of the heap; and she comes in gently, and uncovers his feet, and lies down.
3.8: And it comes to pass, at the middle of the night, that the man trembles, and turns himself, and indeed, a woman is lying at his feet.
3.9: And he says, `Who are you?' and she says, `I am Ruth your handmaid, and you have spread your skirt over your handmaid, for you are a redeemer.'
3.10: And he says, `Blessed are you of Jehovah, my daughter; you have dealt more kindly at the latter end than at the beginning--not to go after the young men, either poor or rich.
3.11: And now, my daughter, fear not, all that you say I do to you, for all the gate of my people does know that you are a virtuous woman.
3.12: And now, surely, true, that I am a redeemer, but also there is a redeemer nearer than I.
3.13: Lodge to night, and it has been in the morning, if he does redeem you, well: he redeems; and if he delight not to redeem you, then I have redeemed you--I; Jehovah lives! lie down till the morning.'
3.14: And she lies down at his feet till the morning, and rises before one does discern another; and he says, `Let it not be known that the woman has come into the floor.'
3.15: And he says, `Give the covering which is on you, and keep hold on it;' and she keeps hold on it, and he measures six measures of barley, and lays it on her; and he goes into the city.
3.16: And she comes in to her mother-in-law, and she says, `Who are you, my daughter?' and she declares to her all that the man has done to her.
3.17: And she says, `These six measures of barley he has given to me, for he said, You do not go in empty to your mother-in-law.'
3.18: And she says, `Sit still, my daughter, till you do know how the matter falls, for the man does not rest except he has completed the matter to-day.'

4.1: And Boaz has gone up to the gate, and sits there, and indeed, the redeemer is passing by of whom Boaz had spoken, and he says, `Turn aside, sit down here, such a one, such a one;' and he turns aside and sits down.
4.2: And he takes ten men of the elders of the city, and says, `Sit down here;' and they sit down.
4.3: And he says to the redeemer, `A portion of the field which is to our brother, to Elimelech, has Naomi sold, who has come back from the fields of Moab;
4.4: and I said, I uncover your ear, saying, Buy before the inhabitants, and before the elders of my people; if you do redeem--redeem, and if none does redeem--declare to me, and I know, for there is none save you to redeem, and I after you.' And he says, I redeem it.'
4.5: And Boaz says, `In the day of your buying the field from the hand of Naomi, then from Ruth the Moabitess, wife of the dead, you have bought it, to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance.'
4.6: And the redeemer says, `I am not able to redeem it for myself, lest I destroy my inheritance; redeem for yourself--you--my right of redemption, for I am not able to redeem.'
4.7: And this is formerly in Israel for redemption and for changing, to establish anything: a man has drawn off his sandal, and given it to his neighbour, and this is the testimony in Israel.
4.8: And the redeemer says to Boaz, `Buy it for yourself,' and draws off his sandal.
4.9: And Boaz says to the elders, and to all the people, `Witnesses are you to-day that I have bought all that is to Elimelech, and all that is to Chilion and Mahlon, from the hand of Naomi;
4.10: and also Ruth the Moabitess, wife of Mahlon, I have bought to myself for a wife, to raise up the name of the dead over his inheritance; and the name of the dead is not cut off from among his brethren, and from the gate of his place; witnesses you are to-day.'
4.11: And all the people who are in the gate say--also the elders--`Witnesses! Jehovah make the woman who is coming in to your house as Rachel and as Leah, both of whom built the house of Israel; and do you virtuously in Ephrathah, and proclaim the Name in Beth-Lehem;
4.12: and let your house be as the house of Pharez (whom Tamar bare to Judah), of the seed which Jehovah does give to you of this young woman.'
4.13: And Boaz takes Ruth, and she becomes his wife, and he goes in to her, and Jehovah gives to her conception, and she bears a son.
4.14: And the women say to Naomi, `Blessed is Jehovah who has not let a redeemer cease to you to-day, and his name is proclaimed in Israel,
4.15: and he has been to you for a restorer of life, and for a nourisher of your old age, for your daughter-in-law who has loved you--who is better to you than seven sons--has borne him.'
4.16: And Naomi takes the lad, and lays him in her bosom, and is to him for a nurse;
4.17: and the neighbouring women give to him a name, saying, `There has been a son born to Naomi,' and they call his name Obed; he is father of Jesse, father of David.
4.18: And these are genealogies of Pharez: Pharez begat Hezron,
4.19: and Hezron begat Ram, and Ram begat Amminidab,
4.20: and Amminidab begat Nahshon, and Nahshon begat Salmon,
4.21: and Salmon begat Boaz, and Boaz begat Obed,
4.22: and Obed begat Jesse, and Jesse begat David.
